question.problem: If $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =0.64$ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha =1.25$, where $\theta $ and $\alpha $ are acute angles measured in degrees, then $\theta +\alpha $ in degrees to one decimal place is{{field-1}}${}^{∘}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find $\theta $ and $\alpha $ we use $arccos$ and $arctan$ respectively. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0.64 \\ \operatorname{arccos}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0.64) \\ \theta  & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0.64)\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha  & =1.25 \\ \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha ) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1.25) \\ \alpha  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1.25).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using a calculator, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta +\alpha  & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0.64)+\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1.25) \\  & =(50.208\,1…)^{∘}+(51.340\,1…)^{∘} \\  & =(101.548\,2…)^{∘} \\  & ≈{101.5}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
